newsitem.title: DUBAI: United Arab Emirates offers to mediate in Sudan.
newsitem.headline: United Arab Emirates offers to mediate in Sudan.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates was ready to mediate in the conflict in Sudan, the president of the Gulf Arab state, Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan, was quoted on Wednesday as saying.

"What is happening in Sudan is an internal matter and if the Sudanese brothers ask us to mediate between the conflicting parties for the interest of the Sudanese brotherly people, we are ready for that," Sheikh Zaid said.
UAE newspapers said the president made his comments during a meeting on Tuesday in Abu Dhabi with Sudanese Cabinet Affairs Minister Salah-Eddin Mohammad Ahmed Karrar.

"If there are parties working for the disintegration of Sudan from outside its borders, this is rejected...The brothers in Sudan must work together as one family to settle their differences and if they could not do that they should ask for help from their Arab brothers to achieve reconciliation," Sheikh Zaid said.
He urged fellow Arab countries "not to keep silent towards events in any Arab country."

A coalition of northern and southern opposition forces began attacking Sudanese army units along the eastern border of the country nine days ago in what they say is a bid to pressure the Khartoum government and pave the way for a popular uprising.
Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir has said Ethiopia and Eritrea are behind the fighting and issued a mobilisation call but both countries deny the charges.
